content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: In this work, authors proposed gated class-attention GCA and feature drift compensation which are applied to ViT to address the exemplar-free class incremental training. Specifically, GCA achieves low forgetting by masking important neurons for each task, and Feature Drift Compensation accommodates feature drift in the backbone when learning new tasks. The experiments show that the proposed approach improves the continual learning performance on the Cifar-100 dataset. On the Tiny ImageNet dataset, the performance is comparable to the SOTA.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
- The authors do what they claim by proposing GCA to mask the critical neurons to prevent forgetting and  Feature Drift Compensation to overcome the feature drift drawbacks of GCA. 
- The idea is easy to follow.
- Ablation study is included to discuss the importance of different components.

Weakness

- The experiments are limited. First of all, the datasets are not interesting, where Cifar-100 and Tiny-ImageNet are very small. Why not conduct experiments on large-scale datasets? Additionally, the Cifar-100 image is in a low resolution, which is not practical. And the proposed method only shows improvement in Cifar-100 data, and there is still a performance gap below the existing work, Evanescent, on Tiny ImageNet data (according to Table2). The comparison to  Evanescent in Table 1 is missing. 

- Another concern is the usage scope. It seems that the proposed GCA and Feature Drift Compensation are for ViTs only. Do they work with other models, as ViTs is not only one model for continual learning? 

- I am curious whether the learned masks incorporate semantic information. For example, masks for different classes but with closed semantics in different stages can have high IoU. Did the authors consider the class semantics when splitting the classes?

- The insights from the T-SNE maps of stage 1 v.s 2 only are limited. Training in more stages, the features for classes in stage 1 would be affected more. I suggested authors also include the feature variance along the stage increment, e,g, stage 1 v.s (2 ,3, 4, 5 …) to show more information on the proposed approach's robustness to prevent forgetting.
 
- Paper writing looks OK but still needs double check and polishing, e.g, the figure 5 captions need rephrasing.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: No code is provided. And there are multiple losses and technical details involved, which might not be easy to reproduce the results
content.summary_of_the_review: Though the idea is easy to follow and the proposed approach shows improvements in continual learning on the Cifar-100 dataset, there is still a performance gap below the existing approaches in the Tiny-ImageNet dataset. Additionally, the chosen data is on a small scale, which makes the contribution less convincing. So, the work is below the acceptance bar.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper addresses the problem of continual learning for Vision Transformers without any exemplars for the previous tasks.
The authors claim that a mask-based gating mechanism with a learnable class token, which is called GCAB (Gated class-attention block), can address the catastrophic forgetting by restricting the update of the masked parameters, which are crucial to the previous tasks.
The authors propose cascaded feature drift compensation, which sequentially projects feature maps into the embedding space of the previous tasks.
In order to handle the increased computational cost, the authors also propose employing a knowledge distillation scheme to build a relatively inexpensive model.
The experimental results on the proposed benchmarks show the effectiveness of the proposed framework compared to the baselines.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
- Strengths
    - While the concept of masking parameters is already proposed in HAT (Serra et al., 2018), incorporating the concept into the ViT is firstly tried and by doing this, the proposed model eliminates the necessity of the task ID, which is a natural goal for continual learning.
    - As a consequence, the proposed framework is applicable to both CIL and TIL settings, without explicit task ID.
    - The distillation procedure works well for the proposed framework with the ability to reduce the cost.
    
- Weaknesses
    - One main drawback of the proposed framework is that it may not be suitable for the longer sequence of tasks, despite the proposed distillation methodology. The proposed distillation method requires a trained teacher, anyway. Training teacher with long sequences requires high computation cost, since the model needs multiple forward passes. The applicability of the model to long incremental sequences is still ambiguous.
    - The notations are somewhat confusing.
        - What is $A$ in Eq (2) ? In HAT, task embedding $e$ is used to generate a mask. So, I guess $A$ is a learnable weight matrix that maps $t$ into some embedding vector, which is similar to $e$. Is it right? It is confusing because attention in Eq (3) shares the same notation, $A$.
    - Discussion for Figure 4 is missing.
        - There should be some explanation or analysis of the results.
    - I wonder about the sensitivity of hyperparameters $\lambda_{pfr}, \lambda_{GCAB}$, since they are too small, especially $\lambda_{pfr}$.
    - Inappropriate claim : The first sentence in third paragraph in the Introduction section.
        - In this paper we propose one of the first exemplar-free methods for class-incremental learning (CIL).
        - → In this paper we propose one of the first exemplar-free methods for class-incremental learning (CIL) **“for Vision Transformers”**.
        - There are already many pieces of literature that handle exemplar-free class-incremental learning for CNNs.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- Clarity : The paper is well-written, but the notations and equations are somewhat confusing.
- Quality : The presentation of the paper is neat.
- Novelty : Two concepts that the authors adopt are already studied, but the authors well modify them and adopts them into ViT architecture.
- Reproducibility : The authors state that they will release the source code if the submission is accepted.
content.summary_of_the_review: Although there could be some controversy with respect to the novelty of the technical contribution (Hard Attention to the Task & Projected Functional Regularization), I think the authors well adopts the existing methods to the ViT architecture with proper modification.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper studies a new method for exemplar-free class incremental training of ViTs. It tried to address the key challenge of exemplar-free continual learning is maintaining plasticity of the learner without causing catastrophic forgetting of previously learned tasks. The model has the key components of gated class-attention, and feature drift compensation. The experiments validate the efficacy of the model.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

The paper is well written, with good motivation and insights.
The results are solid enough to support the claims.

Weakness:

I have some open questions:
1, Does the order of tasks have important impacts to the learning of the model? Say, what are the difference of the tasks organized in an easy-to-hard order, or hard-to-easy order? Or the tasks are organized as the similarities of classes.

2, Can the gating learned in Eq(2)  be visualized to help understand how the model learned?

3. A detailed computational overhead of gated class-attention and ordinary class-attention is needed. 
4. The feature drift compensation seems very inefficient since  all projection networks p_t should be saved. How much memory is needed for saving these projection networks pt.
5. Is the model robust to the λ_{GCAB}? The author should provide some ablation on  λ_{GCAB} to test the model’s sensitivity to hyperparameter.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper develops an exemplar-free continual learning approach based on vision transformers using attention gating, feature drift compensation and distillation.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
STRENGTHS

- Very interesting and relevant topic
- Extensive experiments

WEAKNESSES

- I would say that one of the neat ideas of the paper is to use distillation for continuous learning. However, while this is not such a novel idea, the literature review of the topic is limited. Please extend literature review accordingly [1-4]
- The experimental comparison with exemplar-based methods in Table 1 looks much more impressive than the comparison with the exemplar-free methods in Table 2. Given that the proposed method is exemplar-free, this significantly undermines the convincingness of the experiments. For example, can it be that the exemplar-free methods are significantly more efficient than their exemplar-based counterparts. What if we include a few SOTA exemplar-free methods in Table 1? Will the proposed method still be state of the art? Without the answer to this question, it is hard to recommend the paper for accept, as there is serious doubt about the validity of the experimental framework.
- Task gating is taken from https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.01423.pdf, this is not a novel contribution. I do not understand why this is claimed as a contribution
- It looks like feature drift compensation is a major part of the method, however its description in Section 2.3 in 4 lines surrounding Eq. 7 is very vague. The theoretical justification of feature drift compensation is unclear and is not convincing.

MINOR POINTS

- "reduce forgetting.Mallya et al." missing whitespace
- Tables 2 and 3 are not aligned. This does not look particularly appealing please fix. 

[1] http://home.ustc.edu.cn/~saihui/papers/eccv2018_lifelong.pdf

[2] https://arxiv.org/pdf/1911.03462.pdf

[3] https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.02123

[4] https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-03332046/document
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- I have no reproducibility concerns, since authors promise to release the code upon acceptance
- Originality is moderate as many of the components of the method are borrowed from existing work and compiled together
- Over quality is not great, based on a combination of moderate novelty, unconvincing experimental results and unclear descriptions of key element of the method
- Clarity can be improved as noted in weaknesses section
content.summary_of_the_review:
Overall the paper suffers from a combination of drawbacks including
- Key components are not described clearly and theoretical justification is missing
- novelty is limited 
- empirical results are questionable and unconvincing

Therefore, I recommend to reject the paper

content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
